entities.short_description: Ne Zha 2 (Chinese: 哪吒之魔童闹海; pinyin: Nézhā zhī Mótóng nào hǎi; also known as 哪吒2; Nézhā èr) is a 2025 Chinese animated epic fantasy action-adventure film written and directed by Jiaozi based on the titular mythic figure…
entities.description:
Ne Zha 2 (Chinese: 哪吒之魔童闹海; pinyin: Nézhā zhī Mótóng nào hǎi; also known as 哪吒2; Nézhā èr) is a 2025 Chinese animated epic fantasy action-adventure film written and directed by Jiaozi based on the titular mythic figure of Chinese legend and Xu Zhonglin's 16th-century novel Investiture of the Gods (Fengshen Yanyi). It is the direct sequel to Ne Zha (2019). The film takes up the story of Chinese mythological character Ne Zha and his friend Ao Bing. After a sacrifice, only Ne Zha's body can be recreated, although he carries Ao Bing's spirit within. Ne Zha calls on this spirit in his fight against Master Shen.

Ne Zha 2 was released in theaters across China on 29 January 2025, coinciding with the first day of the Chinese New Year. Like its predecessor, the film received highly positive reviews from critics, and achieved even greater commercial success at a gross of $2.2 billion worldwide against a production budget of US$80 million. Ne Zha 2 broke numerous box office records inside and outside China, including becoming the highest-grossing film in a single box office territory, the highest-grossing animated film, being the first adult animated film in this position, the highest-grossing non-English language film and the first animated film in history to cross the $2 billion mark, as well as being the highest-selling animated film based on ticket sales, overtaking The Jungle Book (1967). It also became the highest-grossing film of 2025 and the fifth-highest-grossing film at the time of its release. A sequel is in development.

entities.name: New Gods: Nezha Reborn
entities.short_description: New Gods: Nezha Reborn (Chinese: 新神榜：哪吒重生) is a 2021 Chinese 3D animated fantasy action film directed by Zhao Ji and written by Mu Chuan, based on the character of Nezha from the Ming dynasty novel Investiture of the…
entities.description:
New Gods: Nezha Reborn (Chinese: 新神榜：哪吒重生) is a 2021 Chinese 3D animated fantasy action film directed by Zhao Ji and written by Mu Chuan, based on the character of Nezha from the Ming dynasty novel Investiture of the Gods. In the film, a steampunk and cyberpunk take on the story, Nezha is reincarnated as Li Yunxiang in the fictional city of Donghai (loosely based on 1920s Shanghai) and must settle a 3,000-year-old grudge with the Dragon Clan. New Gods: Yang Jian was released in 2022 as a sequel to this film.

The film was released in mainland China on 12 February 2021 (Chinese New Year). Netflix acquired global rights to the film except in China, and it was released on the platform on 12 April 2021.

New Gods: Nezha Reborn is not related to the 2019 film Ne Zha; they came from different production companies and have different distributors. Both films are loosely based on the same Ming Dynasty novel.

entities.name: Birthday of the Monkey God
entities.short_description: The Birthday of the Monkey God is a cultural and religious holiday celebrated in Singapore on the 15th or 16th day of the First Lunar Month. The dates on the Western Calendar vary from year to year. It marks the…
entities.description: The Birthday of the Monkey God is a cultural and religious holiday celebrated in Singapore on the 15th or 16th day of the First Lunar Month. The dates on the Western Calendar vary from year to year. It marks the birthday of Sun Wukong, the protagonist in the classical novel Journey to the West. The popular celebratory customs associated with the Birthday of the Monkey God have both secular and religious (Taoist) themes. This is not to be confused with the Monkey King Festival celebrated in China on the 16th day of the Eighth Lunar Calendar.

entities.name: Cloud tea
entities.short_description: Cloud tea (Chinese: 雲雾茶; pinyin: yún wù chá; pronounced [y̌n û ʈʂʰǎ]) is a Chinese green tea that originally comes from Nanyue Mountain. It is named for the clouds of Le Mountain (南岳山; nányuè shān) where it is produced.…
entities.description: Cloud tea (Chinese: 雲雾茶; pinyin: yún wù chá; pronounced [y̌n û ʈʂʰǎ]) is a Chinese green tea that originally comes from Nanyue Mountain. It is named for the clouds of Le Mountain (南岳山; nányuè shān) where it is produced. In ancient times, it was called Le tea. During the Tang dynasty, it was used as tribute to the emperor. Cloud tea grows in the area of Guangji Temple, Tiefu Temple and Huagai Peak at an altitude of 800 to 1,100 metres (2,600 to 3,600 ft) with a mild and wet climate. Meanwhile, rich organic matter in the soil is extremely suitable for the tea's growth. The Chinese great tea master, Lu Yu in the Tang dynasty, once mentioned it in The Classic of Tea, which provides for the reputation of cloud tea in Le Mountain. In general, it is famous not only for its thin leaf and beauty, but also the fresh colour, cool taste and attractive smell. It has won an outstanding reputation in both Hunan Province and abroad.

entities.name: Douzhanopterus
entities.short_description: Douzhanopterus is an extinct genus of monofenestratan pterosaur from the Late Jurassic of Liaoning, China. It contains a single species, D. zhengi, named by Wang et al. in 2017. In many respects, it represents a…
entities.description: Douzhanopterus is an extinct genus of monofenestratan pterosaur from the Late Jurassic of Liaoning, China. It contains a single species, D. zhengi, named by Wang et al. in 2017. In many respects, it represents a transitional form between basal pterosaurs and the more specialized pterodactyloids; for instance, its tail is intermediate in length, still being about twice the length of the femur but relatively shorter compared to that of the more basal Wukongopteridae. Other intermediate traits include the relative lengths of the neck vertebrae and the retention of two, albeit reduced, phalanx bones in the fifth digit of the foot. Phylogenetically, Douzhanopterus is nested between the wukongopterids and Propterodactylus, which is similar to Douzhanopterus in many respects but approaches pterodactyloids more closely elsewhere.

entities.name: Drunken Monkey
entities.short_description: Drunken Monkey Form or Drunken Monkey Pole Form of Kung Fu is a Chinese martial art, a variation of the Monkey Style.
entities.description:
Drunken Monkey Form or Drunken Monkey Pole Form of Kung Fu is a Chinese martial art, a variation of the Monkey Style.

This style is different from Zui Quan (Drunken Fist), as the practitioner is imitating gestures of an intoxicated monkey, rather than a human fighter.

Drunken Monkey does not begin with drunken-like gestures, but rather the drunken aspect enters the forms in the middle-section when the practitioner plays the movements of a monkey drinking stolen wine.

The Drunken Monkey style is visually completely different when compared to Zui Quan and is shorter in sequence. This style, however, is considered more artistically beautiful, acrobatic and agile compared to Zui Quan. This does not necessarily mean that it is more or less effective in actual combat.

Contrary to claims in movies, actually being drunk does not improve drunken monkey or drunken fist. It is based on the concept of imitating being drunk; actually being drunk is not required and may impair one's speed and ability to perform complex movements.

entities.name: Monkey mind
entities.short_description: The term monkey mind or mind monkey originates from Chinese xīnyuán or Sino-Japanese shin'en (心猿), a word that literally means "heart-mind monkey." It is a Buddhist concept that describes a state of restlessness,…
entities.description: The term monkey mind or mind monkey originates from Chinese xīnyuán or Sino-Japanese shin'en (心猿), a word that literally means "heart-mind monkey." It is a Buddhist concept that describes a state of restlessness, capriciousness, and lack of control in one's thoughts. This "mind monkey" metaphor is not only found in Buddhist writings such as Chan or Zen, Consciousness-only, Pure Land, and Shingon, but it has also been adopted in Taoism, Neo-Confucianism, Chinese poetry, theater, and literature. The expression "monkey mind" commonly appears in two reversible four-character idioms paired with yima or iba (意馬), which means "idea horse": Chinese xinyuanyima (心猿意馬) and Japanese ibashin'en (意馬心猿) illustrate the interconnectedness of a restless mind and wandering thoughts. The "Monkey King" Sun Wukong in the classic Chinese novel Journey to the West is an iconic personification of feeling indecisive and unsettled.

entities.name: Monkey King Festival
entities.short_description: The Monkey King Festival (Chinese: 齊天大聖千秋) is celebrated in Hong Kong on the 16th day of the eighth Lunar month of the Chinese calendar, corresponding to September according to the Common era calendar, a day after the…
entities.description: The Monkey King Festival (Chinese: 齊天大聖千秋) is celebrated in Hong Kong on the 16th day of the eighth Lunar month of the Chinese calendar, corresponding to September according to the Common era calendar, a day after the Mid Autumn Festival. The origin of the festival is traced to the epic 16th century novel Journey to the West (Xiyou Ji, 西遊記) written by the Chinese novelist Wu Cheng'en (1500–1582) during the Ming dynasty (1368–1644). The novel brings out the concept of immortality from Taoism and rebirth from Buddhism. The monkey Sun Wukong, a character in the novel, is the featured figure of the festival.

entities.name: Monkey Kung Fu
entities.short_description: Monkey kung fu or Hóu Quán (猴拳, "monkey fist") is a Chinese martial art which utilizes ape or monkey-like movements as part of its technique.
entities.description:
Monkey kung fu or Hóu Quán (猴拳, "monkey fist") is a Chinese martial art which utilizes ape or monkey-like movements as part of its technique.

Northern Chinese martial arts such as Northern Praying Mantis and Wuzuquan incorporate some of the techniques from monkey kung fu.

entities.name: Ruyi Jingu Bang
entities.short_description: The staff is initially described as a pillar of black iron, twenty feet in height and the width of a barrel. After shrinking to the size Wukong mainly uses when wielding, it is only a little taller than him, and as…
entities.description:
The staff is initially described as a pillar of black iron, twenty feet in height and the width of a barrel. After shrinking to the size Wukong mainly uses when wielding, it is only a little taller than him, and as thick as a rice bowl. The weapon is banded with a gold ring at each of its ends. An inscription runs along its body, denoting its name as the "Compliant Golden-Hooped Staff" and its weight as "thirteen thousand five hundred catties", which is approximately 7,960 kg (17,550 lbs). Due to its huge size and monstrously heavy weight, few beings besides Wukong are able to even lift the staff.

The inscription indicates that the staff follows the commands of its owner, shrinking or growing to his whim, and make copies of itself.

The Ruyi Jingu Bang was originally one of the massive nails that Yu the Great used to set the depth of rivers and seas in order to prevent flooding. It was placed in the treasury of the Dragon Palace of the East Sea.

When Sun Wukong went to the palace to find a weapon he could use, the Ruyi Jingu Bang began glowing auspiciously. The Dragon Queen noticed this and suggested to her husband Ao Guang to give the rod to Sun Wukong after every other weapon in their armoury proved too light for him.

entities.name: Tiong Bahru Monkey God Temple
entities.short_description: Qi Tian Gong (simplified Chinese: 齐天宫; traditional Chinese: 齊天宮), commonly referred to as the Tiong Bahru Monkey God Temple, is a Taoist temple in Tiong Bahru, Singapore.
entities.description:
Qi Tian Gong (simplified Chinese: 齐天宫; traditional Chinese: 齊天宮), commonly referred to as the Tiong Bahru Monkey God Temple, is a Taoist temple in Tiong Bahru, Singapore.

Reportedly the first temple in the country dedicated to the Journey to the West character Sun Wukong (also known as the Monkey King), Qi Tian Gong was established in 1920. It was originally located in an attap dwelling but relocated to a rented shophouse at 44 Eng Hoon Street in 1938. In 1985, the temple's trustees bought over the shophouse. The temple houses more than ten statues of the Monkey King, some of which date back to the 1910s.

As part of the temple's yearly festivities, devotees will walk around Tiong Bahru with Monkey King idols. Joss paper will also be burnt while the burning area is purified with a snake-headed whip. Until 2018, the temple also had a medium who would be possessed by the Monkey God.

entities.description: Wukong Bicycle (Chinese: 悟空) was a bicycle-sharing company based in Chongqing, China. The company operated a fleet of 1,200 bicycles in Chongqing from January to July 2017, ceasing operations after 90 percent of their bicycles were reported missing.

entities.name: Yellow Wind Demon
entities.short_description: The is a demon who dwelled on Yellow Wind Ridge.
entities.description:
The is a demon who dwelled on Yellow Wind Ridge.

The Yellow Wind Demon wore a reflective gold helmet with pheasant-tail tassels, a yellow silk robe topped with a gold cuirass, a dragon-like sash with several brilliant hues, suede boots dyed with locust flowers, and an embroidered kilt decked with willow leaves. He apparently bore a resemblance to Erlang Shen.

The Yellow Wind Demon was once a yellow-furred marten that dwelt on Vulture Peak, which gained human form through spirit cultivation. It drank some holy oil from the Thunderclap Monastery and fled, fearing retribution. The Tathagata Buddha, merciful, sent the Bodhisattva Lingji to defeat the Yellow Wind Demon using the Wind-Arresting Pearl and Flying Dragon Precious Staff, then forced it to only reside on Yellow Wind Ridge.

Afterwards, the Yellow Wind Demon amassed a small army of demons under its control. One of these demons, the Tiger Vanguard, managed to capture the pilgrim Tang Sanzang. This provoked the ire of Sun Wukong, who attacked the Yellow Wind Cave.

entities.name: Zhu Bajie
entities.short_description: Zhu Bajie is an anthropomorphic pig demon. He has an ugly face covered in stubby black hairs, with a long snout and huge ears. He wore a cyan cotton shirt and kept a spotted cotton handkerchief wrapped around his head.
entities.description:
Zhu Bajie is an anthropomorphic pig demon. He has an ugly face covered in stubby black hairs, with a long snout and huge ears. He wore a cyan cotton shirt and kept a spotted cotton handkerchief wrapped around his head.

Zhu Bajie was once a human who was slothful and indolent, but one day he met a Daoist immortal, who convinced him to change his ways. Through alchemical study and spirit cultivation, the two became immortals and ascended to Heaven. In Heaven, he was assigned as the Heavenly Canopy Martial, who commanded a navy of 80,000 heavenly sailors.

In the aftermath of Sun Wukong's rampage through Heaven, he served as a messenger and asked the Tathagata Buddha to stay so the Jade Emperor could see him. Sometime later, he drunkenly tried to seduce the goddess Chang'e. The Jade Emperor punished him to be reincarnated as a mortal on Earth.

While his spirit was searching for a proper place to reincarnate, it accidentally passed through the womb of an old pig and was born as its child. He bit his mother to death and killed the rest of the litter, then killed and ate the owners of the farm he was incarnated into. He then passed the years killing an eating any travellers.

entities.name: Sun Wukong
entities.short_description: Sun Wukong is a monkey born from a magical rock on top of Flowers and Fruit Mountain. When his eyes moved, two beams of golden light shot towards the Heavenly Palace and surprise the Jade Emperor. On the mountain, the…
entities.description:
Sun Wukong is a monkey born from a magical rock on top of Flowers and Fruit Mountain. When his eyes moved, two beams of golden light shot towards the Heavenly Palace and surprise the Jade Emperor. On the mountain, the monkey befriends various animals and joins a group of other monkeys. They decide to seek the stream's source and climb the mountain to a waterfall. They declare that whoever goes through the waterfall, finds the stream's source, and comes out again will become their king.

In search of a weapon, he travels to the oceans and gets the Ruyi Jingu Bang which stabilizes the Four Seas and is the Treasure of the Eastern Dragon King. After rebelling against heaven and being imprisoned under Five Finger Mountain for 500 years by Buddha, he later accompanies the monk Tang Sanzang on a journey to retrieve Buddhist sutras from India. At the end of the journey, Wukong is granted the title of Victorious Fighting Buddha and ascends to Buddhahood.

entities.name: Tang Sanzang
entities.short_description: While his mother Yin Wenjiao was pregnant with him, his father Chen Guangrui was murdered by Liu Hong, who wanted both his mother to marry him and his father's offical position. When he was born, the Old Man of the…
entities.description:
While his mother Yin Wenjiao was pregnant with him, his father Chen Guangrui was murdered by Liu Hong, who wanted both his mother to marry him and his father's offical position. When he was born, the Old Man of the South Pole instructed his mother to set him out to drift. She wrote his lineage on his bundle, then bit off the tip of one of his toes so that he could be identified.

The baby drifted to the banks of the Gold Mountain Monastery, where the Buddhist monks found it. He was named River Float because of this, and was later given the Buddhist name Xuanzang. He excelled at his studies, and when he learned of his heritage he exposed Liu Hong and had him executed. He then returned to the Gold Mountain Monastery.

entities.short_description: Vilambā has a face like autumn before frost. She wore a five flower-patterned silk cap, a knitted gold robe, a double-tasseled silk sash, and cloud-patterned phoenix-beaked shoes.
entities.description:
Vilambā has a face like autumn before frost. She wore a five flower-patterned silk cap, a knitted gold robe, a double-tasseled silk sash, and cloud-patterned phoenix-beaked shoes.

Vilambā had not left her cave on Purple Cloud Mountain in 300 years, so was surprised when Sun Wukong came to ask her for help with defeating the Hundred-Eyed Demon Lord. She easily subjugated the Demon Lord using a needle to paralyse him, then forced him to become the guard of her cave.

Like her son the Sun Rooster of Hairy Head, Vilambā has the ability to subjugate any kind of insect.

entities.short_description: The , or , served as the steed of Tang Sanzang during his pilgrimage.
entities.description:
The , or , served as the steed of Tang Sanzang during his pilgrimage.

The White Dragon Horse is the third son of Ao Run, the Dragon King of the West Sea. He once accidentally set a fire to Ao Run's palace, destroying a pearl that was a gift from the Jade Emperor.

He was hung up in the sky and was to be executed, but the Bodhisattva Guanyin came across him and had the execution canceled in exchange for the White Dragon Horse helping out the pilgrim whose route she was scouting. She had him wait in at Eagle Grief Stream for them.

The Jade Dragon waited in the stream, but when the pilgrim Tang Sanzang came he didn’t recognise him, eating his horse. After fighting Sun Wukong, the Jade Dragon begged Guanyin for forgiveness, who transformed him into the White Dragon Horse to replace the one he ate.

entities.short_description: Maitreya in journey to the west.
entities.description:
When Maitreya left to attend the Festival of Original Commencement, he left his pageboy Yellow-Browed Great King to take care of his palace. Instead, the Great King stole his Golden Cymbals and Human Seed Bag.

Maitreya came to retrieve his treasures and met with Sun Wukong, who the Great King had just defeated. The two came up with a plan where Maitreya posed as a melon farmer and fed the Yellow-Browed Great King a melon which was actually Sun Wukong in disguise.

entities.name: Nezha
entities.short_description: Nezha in journey to the west.
entities.description:
Prince Nezha is a young boy with an air of elegance and intelligence. His hair in tufts barely covers his scalp, and his cloak doesn’t cover his shoulders.

When Prince Nezha was born, he had the character 哪 emblazoned on his left hand and 吒 on his right. On the third morning after he was born, he decided to go bathing in the ocean and ended up overturning the Dragon King's palace, then tried to kill a dragon to make its tendons into a belt.

Fearing his son would become a monster, King Li Jing attempted to kill him. Nezha was so enraged he killed himself to give his mother back his skin and his father back his bones.

Nezha's soul then went to the Western Continent to beg for mercy from the Tathagata Buddha, who restored Nezha to life using lotus stems for bones and leaves for skin. Nezha became so powerful that he subjugated the demons of 96 caves and decided to seek vengeance on his family.

entities.name: Nüwa
entities.short_description: Nüwa, also read Nügua, is a mother goddess, culture hero, and/or member of the Three Sovereigns of Chinese mythology. She is a goddess in Chinese folk religion, Chinese Buddhism, Confucianism and Taoism. She is credited…
entities.description:
Nüwa, also read Nügua, is a mother goddess, culture hero, and/or member of the Three Sovereigns of Chinese mythology. She is a goddess in Chinese folk religion, Chinese Buddhism, Confucianism and Taoism. She is credited with creating humanity and repairing the Pillar of Heaven.

As creator of mankind, she molded humans individually by hand with yellow clay. In other stories where she fulfills this role, she only created nobles and/or the rich out of yellow soil. The stories vary on the other details about humanity's creation, but it was a tradition commonly believed in ancient China that she created commoners from brown mud. A story holds that she was tired when she created "the rich and the noble", so all others, or "cord-made people", were created from her "dragg[ing] a string through mud".

In the Huainanzi, there is a description of a great battle between deities that broke the pillars supporting Heaven and caused great devastation. There was great flooding, and Heaven had collapsed. Nüwa was the one who patched the holes in Heaven with five colored stones, and she used the legs of a tortoise to mend the pillars.

There are many instances of her in literature across China which detail her in creation stories, and today, she remains a figure important to Chinese culture. She is one of the most venerated Chinese goddesses alongside Guanyin and Mazu.

In Chinese mythology, the goddess Nüwa is a legendary progenitor of all human beings. She also creates a magic stone. Her husband Fu Xi is suggested to be the progenitor of divination and the patron saint of numbers.

entities.name: Old Man of the South Pole
entities.short_description: Old Man of the South Pole in journey to the west.
entities.description:
The is an immortal in charge of governing the [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canopus Pole Star] and assigning the death dates of people.

Whenever a living being is born, be they mortal or immortal, the Old Man of the South Pole writes their preordained death date in the Register of Life and Death.

When Sun Wukong was sentenced to be executed, the Star Spirit of the South Pole oversaw it. He had both the Department of Fire and Department of Thunder attack him, but it was ineffective.

In a dream, the Star Spirit instructed Yin Wenjiao to set her baby (who would become Tang Sanzang) adrift on a plank of wood so that her forced husband Liu Hong would not kill him.

entities.name: Princess Iron Fan
entities.short_description: Princess Iron Fan in journey to the west.
entities.description:
Princess Iron Fan wore a flower-patterned scarf around her head, a priestly brocade robe, two tiger tendons as a belt, a silk skirt, trousers with gold fringes, and phoenix-bill shoes. She wielded a pair of blue swords.

Princess Iron Fan was the wife of the Bull Demon King and the mother of Red Boy. The Bull Demon King later divorced her to marry Princess Jade-Face after she offered him a great deal of money.

Every ten years, the people who live near the Flaming Mountains come to Jade Cloud Mountain to beg her to temporarily extinguish the fire on the mountain with her magical Banana-Leaf Fan so they can grow crops.

When Sun Wukong comes to her looking to extinguish the Flaming Mountains, she attacks him for getting Red Boy into trouble, using her Banana-Leaf Fan to send him flying. He returns soon after, and due to the Wind-Arresting Elixir she can’t blow him away again.

entities.description:
The Queen Mother of the West organised a feast for the gods and ordered her attendants, the Seven Fairies, to pick divine peaches from the Peach Tree Garden. The Seven Fairies returned to the Queen Mother after having spent a day frozen by Sun Wukong, who had eaten many of the peaches. The Queen Mother then reported this to her husband.

entities.name: Red Boy
entities.short_description: Red Boy in journey to the west.
entities.description:
Red Boy has powder-white skin, lips that look like they’ve been painted red, immaculate black hair, and eyebrows shaped like new moons. He wore nothing but an armoured kilt emblazoned with the images of phoenixes and dragons.

Red Boy is the son of the Bull Demon King and Princess Iron Fan, and was raised by a rakshasi.

When Tang Sanzang came by Roaring Mountain, Red Boy disguised himself as a young boy tied up on the road. Sun Wukong didn’t fall for his disguise, so Red Boy transformed into a whirlwind and kidnapped Sanzang before anyone could react.

The pilgrims found Fire Wind Cave and challenged Red Boy, but he used the True Fire of Samadhi to overwhelm them. When Zhu Bajie went to get help from Guanyin, Red Boy disguised himself as her and trapped him.

entities.short_description: Seven Fairies in journey to the west.
entities.description:
The are a group of attendants of the Queen Mother of the West.

The Seven Fairies went to harvest peaches from the Peach Tree Garden and stumbled upon Sun Wukong, who was supposed to be protecting the grove, sleeping after eating some of the peaches. When Sun Wukong found out he hadn't been invited to the banquet, he used a spell that froze the Seven Fairies in place for an entire day.

entities.name: Sha Wujing
entities.short_description: Sha Wujing in journey to the west.
entities.description:
Sha Wujing is a river demon with indigo skin, tussled and flame-like hair, and bright red eyes that shon like lamps. He wore a cape of light yellow goose downs, a belt of white reeds, and a sash of nine skulls strung with a rope.

Sha Wujing was once a human who had been strong since birth and became renowned as a gallant hero. He wanted to learn the Dao, so he travelled the world as a beggar until he'd gone everywhere a thousand times. Only then did he find an immortal to teach him the art of spirit cultivation. He became an immortal and rose to Heaven, where he was given the title Curtain-Raising General.

Due to his carelessness, he accidentally broke a crystal vase belonging to the Queen Mother of the West during a banquet. The Jade Emperor punished him with eight hundred lashes, banished him to Earth, transformed him into a river demon, and sent a flying sword to cut him over a hundred times every seven days. And due to not having any food, he was forced to kill and eat travellers.

Eventually, the Bodhisattva Guanyin came over the Flowing Sand River. Sha Wujing attacked her before realising who she was, and then begged her to absolve him of his crimes. She gave him the name Sha Wujing and promised he would be pardoned if he helped the pilgrim whose route she was scouting when he arrived.

entities.name: Six-Eared Macaque
entities.short_description: Six-Eared Macaque in journey to the west.
entities.description:
The is a clairvoyant monkey who impersonated Sun Wukong.

The Six-Eared Macaque is one of four beings that don’t fall into the usual ten categories of life. The other three are the Spirit Intellect Stone Monkey, the Red-Buttock Baboon, and the Interconnected-Arm Gibbon.

When Sun Wukong was cast out, the Six-Eared Macaque tried to take his place in disguise, but when Tang Sanzang rejected him he assaulted him and stole his luggage. He then plotted to complete the pilgrimage himself by having other monkey spirits impersonate the other pilgrims.

When the real Sun Wukong was informed of his imposter's existence, they fought evenly matched through the universe. They fought through Mount Potalaka, Heaven, and the Underworld without any god being able to discern their identity. Finally, they came to the Thunderclap Monastery, where the Tathagata Buddha successfully identified the Six-Eared Macaque. He was captured, and Sun Wukong killed him in rage.

entities.name: Ao Guang
entities.short_description: Ao Guang in journey to the west.
entities.description:
The monkey king Sun Wukong obtained his Ruyi Jingu Bang, a magically expanding, gold-ringed iron rod weapon, from Ao Guang. This weapon was originally a tool for measuring the depth of sea water used by Yu the Great in his flood control and treatment efforts; hence its ability to vary its shape and length. After Yu left, it remained in the sea and became the "Pillar holding down the sea", an unmovable treasure of the undersea palace of Ao Guang.

One of Wukong's senior advisors had told him to seek out the dragon-king in order to get a powerful weapon befitting his skill. In the dragon palace, he tried out several kinds of heavenly weapons, many of which bent or completely broke as he wielded them. Ao Guang's wife then suggested the Ruyi Jingu Bang, stating that some time prior the iron rod had begun to emit a strange heavenly light and that she believed the Monkey King was destined to obtain it. When Wukong neared the pillar, it began to glow, signifying that the Monkey King was its true owner. It obediently listened to his commands and shrank to a manageable size so Wukong could wield it effectively. This awed the dragons and threw the sea into confusion, the Monkey King having removed the only thing controlling the ebb and flow of the ocean's tides. In addition to the magic staff, Wukong also forced Ao Guang to give him other magical gifts; including golden chain mail, a phoenix-feather cap, and cloud-walking boots.

Wukong solicits Ao Guang's aid later in the journey to overcome Red Boy, a demon that had captured Tang Sanzang. Ao Guang provides torrential rain in an attempt to stop Red Boy's fire but the fire could not be stopped by ordinary water. Ao Guang returns to the East Ocean unable to help Wukong defeat Red Boy. In a later adventure, Ao Guang again shows deference to Wukong and assists Wukong in a rain-making contest and creating an elixir.

entities.short_description: Ao Run in journey to the west.
entities.description:
Ao Run and the other Dragon Kings were summoned by Ao Guang when Sun Wukong demanded to be given a new set of clothes. Ao Run convinced his brother, Ao Qin, that Sun Wukong was too dangerous to fight, and that they sound comply with his demands, then alert Heaven to arrest him. Ao Run gave Sun Wukong his Gold Chain Armor.

entities.name: Barefoot Immortal
entities.short_description: Barefoot Immortal in journey to the west.
entities.description:
The is a revered immortal invited up to Heaven for a banquet.

The Barefoot Immortal was invited up to Heaven to attend a banquet held by the Queen Mother of the West, but when he arrived Sun Wukong tricked him into going to the Hall of Universal Brightness first instead of the Jade Pool.

The Barefoot Immortal rode on propitious cloud, and when he arrives somewhere clouds of many colours streak across the sky and the cry of a stork makes the heavens shake. He wears a talisman around his waist which wards off birth and death.

entities.name: Bull Demon King
entities.short_description: Bull Demon King in journey to the west.
entities.description:
The is the old sworn brother of Sun Wukong, the father of Red Boy, and the ex-husband of Princess Iron Fan.

The Bull Demon King met Sun Wukong during his travels around the world after becoming immortal and became sworn brothers with him and five other demon kings. Sun Wukong frequently hosted extravagant banquets for them. After Sun Wukong took the title Great Sage Equal to Heaven, the Bull Demon King began calling himself the Great Sage that Pacifies Heaven.

Sometime later, the Bull Demon King married Princess Iron Fan and fathered Red Boy. When Princess Jade-Face inherited a vast amount of money from her father, she used it to convince the Bull Demon King to divorce Princess Iron Fan and marry her instead.

Sun Wukong came to Thunder-Accumulating Mountain to ask him to convince Princess Iron Fan to lend him her Banana-Leaf Fan. He was enraged due to Sun Wukong getting his son Red Boy in trouble and fought him. He abruptly called off the fight after being given an invitation by the All-Saints Dragon King.

entities.name: Erlang Shen
entities.short_description: Erlang Shen in journey to the west.
entities.description:
Erlang Shen projected a refined and noble visage. His long ears hung down to his shoulders and his eyes shon. He wore a hat with three peaks and the images of phoenixes flying, a pale goose-yellow robe, boots lined with gold cloth, socks with dragons coiled around them, and a jade belt decorated with eight jewels.

In his giant form, he had a black face, long fangs, bright red hair, and overall looked monstrous.

Erlang's mother was the Jade Emperor's sister, Princess Yaoji, who was imprisoned under Mount Tao because she violated the Heavenly Rules by marrying a human named Yang Tianyou. Many years later, Erlang Shen cleaved the mountain using his axe, hoping to set his mother free. He did successfully rescue his mother after he chased away the sun by carrying a mountain on his back. In latter adventures he became renowned for killing the Twin Phoenixes of Zongluo and the Eight Bogies, and formed the Six Brothers of Mount Mei.

At Guanyin's suggestion, the Jade Emperor had Erlang summoned to fight Sun Wukong. The two were evenly matched and fought for three hundred rounds, with Erlang's phoenix eye finding him whenever he transformed. Eventually, Laozi knocked Sun Wukong down with his Diamond Cutter, allowing for Erlang and his sworn brothers to bind him.

entities.name: Four Heavenly Kings
entities.short_description: Four Heavenly Kings in journey to the west.
entities.description:
The are a group of gods responsible for governing over the four cardinal directions.

When the Nine Stars failed to defeat Sun Wukong, King Li Jing, Prince Nezha, the Four Heavenly Kings, and the Twenty-Eight Constellations were sent all at once to attack him. They battled Sun Wukong and his monkey army for an entire day, but were forced to retreat by nightfall.

entities.name: Guanyin
entities.short_description: Guanyin in journey to the west.
entities.description:
Guanyin and her apprentice Muzha went up to Heaven for the annual peach festival and found it in disarray due to the chaos caused by Sun Wukong. Guanyin suggested summoning Erlang Shen, who was successful able to capture Sun Wukong.

400 years later, Guanyin was chosen by the Tathagata Buddha to select a worthy monk to make a pilgrimage to Thunderclap Monastery and bring the Tripitaka to the Southern Continent. As she flew there, she encountered Sha Wujing, Zhu Bajie, the White Dragon Horse, and Sun Wukong in turn. She made each of them promise to aid the pilgrim in the future.

Guanyin arrived in the city of Chang'an in the Tang Empire, where she disguised herself as a ragged woman selling a beautiful cassock. She gave chief minister Xiao Yu the cassock to give to the most virtuous monk he knew, and he chose Tang Sanzang. Guanyin then appeared to Tang Sanzang while he was giving an address and tasked him with the pilgrimage.

Guanyin assisted the pilgrims frequently during their pilgrimage such as by helping trick the Black Wind Demon, who she recruited as the guard of Mount Potalaka, resurrecting the Ginseng Fruit Tree, and subduing Red Boy, who she forced to become her apprentice.

entities.name: Hundred-Eyed Demon Lord
entities.short_description: Hundred-Eyed Demon Lord in journey to the west.
entities.description:
The is a demon who once dwelt in Yellow Flower Abbey.

The Hundred-Eyed Demon Lord could pass as a regular human and wore a red cap lacquered with gold, a luminous black robe, a yellow sash, and green cloud-patterned shoes. Beneath his shirt is hidden one thousand eyes growing from his ribs.

The Hundred-Eyed Demon Lord studied the art of Daoism alongside seven Spider Spirits, and eventually became the proprietor of Yellow Flower Abbey.

After being defeated by a group of pilgrims, the Spider Spirits came to Yellow Flower Abbey seeking sanctuary. Coincidentally, the pilgrims also came to Yellow Flower Abbey, and the Demon Lord conspired to poison their tea using an extremely potent poison in his possession.

entities.name: Jade Emperor
entities.short_description: In the myths and folk religion of Chinese culture, the Jade Emperor or Yudi is one of the representations of the primordial god.
entities.description:
In the myths and folk religion of Chinese culture, the Jade Emperor or Yudi is one of the representations of the primordial god.

In Taoist theology, he is the assistant of Yuanshi Tianzun, who is one of the Three Pure Ones, the three primordial emanations of the Tao. However, some Taoists in history were skeptical of his benevolence because his buildings and infrastructure in heaven and earth were sometimes seen as interfering with the many natural laws or dao.

He is often identified with Śakra in Chinese Buddhist cosmology and identified with Yu the Great in Chinese mythology.

The Jade Emperor is known by many names, including Yu; Heavenly Grandfather (Chinese: 天公, romanized: Tiāngōng), which originally meant "Heavenly Duke" (and which is used by commoners); the Jade Lord; the Highest Emperor; and Great Emperor of Jade (玉皇上帝, Yu Huang Shangdi, or 玉皇大帝, Yu Huang Dadi).

entities.name: Laozi
entities.short_description: Laozi in journey to the west.
entities.description:
Laozi went out to preach the Tao with Dipankara, and when he returned home to the Tushita Heavenly Palace he found that Sun Wukong had eaten his entire supply of Golden Pills of the Nine Transformations.

When the gods had trouble arresting Sun Wukong for his crimes, Laozi threw his Diamond Cutter at Sun Wukong to knock him to the ground, where Erlang Shen and the Six Brothers of Mount Mei were able to capture him.

entities.description:
Lingji was tasked by the Tathagata Buddha with defeating the Yellow Wind Demon, and was given the Wind-Arresting Pearl and Flying Dragon Precious Staff. He successfully confined the Yellow Wind Demon to Yellow Wind Ridge.

When Tang Sanzang was captured by the Yellow Wind Demon, Sun Wukong fetched Lingji, who used the Flying Dragon Precious Staff to transform the demon back into its true form, a yellow-furred mink.

entities.name: Mahamayuri
entities.short_description: Mahamayuri in journey to the west.
entities.description:
When the universe was still forming, a phoenix's egg was inspirited by the creative aura and hatched both the Golden-Winged Great Peng and a giant peacock that could suck in prey from miles away.

Before he attained Buddhahood, Siddhartha Gautama was swallowed whole by the giant peacock and had to cut himself out of its stomach. He wanted to kill the peacock, but the elder Buddhas advised him that the peacock was now his spiritual mother. This peacock later reincarnated as Mahamayuri.

Two of Magamayuri's peacock children were killed by the prince of Scarlet-Purple Kingdom when he was young. As punishment, it was ordained that he should spend three years separated from his wife.

entities.name: Demon king of confusion
entities.short_description: Demon king of confusion in journey to the west.
entities.description:
During the time when Sun Wukong was off on Spirit Tower Heart Mountain training to become an immortal, the Demon King of Confusion began frequently invading Flowers and Fruit Mountain to take the monkeys there his prisoners. When Sun Wukong returned, he sought out the Demon King and easily overwhelmed him by duplicating himself. He was beaten to a pulp and then had his head sliced in two by his own sword.

The Demon King of Confusion stood thirty feet tall and was ten spans wide, and he looked fearsome. He wore a black gold helmet, a dark silk robe, a black iron vest tied with leather straps, and pair of well-made boots.

When coming and going somewhere, the Demon King of Confusion surrounded himself with mist, wind, rain, thunder, and lightning to conceal himself. He wielded a large, gleaming sword during combat.

entities.name: Liu Boqin
entities.short_description: Liu Boqin in journey to the west.
entities.description:
Liu Boqin wore a cap of white leopard skin, a robe of lamb's wool with a dark silk brocade, a belt with an ornate lion for a buckle, and suede boots. He was muscular and had a wild beard. He carried with him a steel trident and a bow with poisoned arrows.

Liu Boqin and his family make a living killing and skinning tigers on Double-Fork Ridge where they live. Boqin found Tang Sanzang and took him to the mountain village he called home, and though Sanzang was disgusted by Boqin's occupation, he remained courteous. After Sanzang accidentally purified the ghost of Boqin's father while reciting his sutras in the morning, Boqin accompanied him on his journey as far as the Mountain of Two Frontiers.

entities.name: All-Saints Dragon King
entities.description:
The was a Dragon King who resides in Jade Wave Lagoon.

The All-Saints Dragon King was originally pious, but after his daughter Princess All-Saints married the Nine-Headed Insect he was convinced to steal a [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/%C5%9Aar%C4%ABra sarira] from the Sacrifice Kingdom.

One day, the All-Saints Dragon King held a banquet in Jade Wave Lagoon and invited the Bull Demon King to attend.

Soon after, Sun Wukong and Zhu Bajie came to Jade Wave Lagoon demanding the return of the stolen sarira. The Nine-Headed Insect captured Zhu Bajie, but he escaped. Feigning retreat, Zhu Bajie lured the Dragon King out of the water, where his was killed in one blow by Sun Wukong.

entities.name: Antelope Power Immortal
entities.description:
The was one of a trio of supposed Daoist immortals who became preceptors of the Slow Cart Kingdom.

When the Slow Cart Kingdom suffered from drought, the Tiger Power Immortal, Elk Power Immortal, and Antelope Power Immortal arrived and brought rain. They were given the position of preceptor, and used their new station to enslave every Buddhist in the kingdom.

After a ceremony, the three immortals found that all their food offerings had been miraculously eaten. Thinking that the Three Pure Ones did it, they prayed to be given golden elixir by them, and a statue advised them to leave a bottle in the room for it to fill. When the immortals tasted the "golden elixir", they quickly realised it was urine, and the statue turned out to be Sun Wukong in disguise.

The immortals wanted the pilgrims to be enslaved like the other Buddhists, but the king couldn’t figure out who to side with and ordered a series of competitions. The Antelope Power Immortal assisted the Tiger Power Immortal by sending a bedbug to irritate Tang Sanzang as he meditated, but they failed.

Ao Qin gave Sun Wukong his Phoenix Feather Cap.

entities.name: Black Wind Demon
entities.description:
The is a bear demon who dwelled on Black Wind Mountain.

The Black Wind Demon has black-coloured skin like a coal miner and golden pupils that flash like lightning. He wears a bowl-like helmet made of dark steel, a shining black-gold cuirass, a black silk robe with wide wind-bagging sleeves, dark green sashes with long tassels, and black leather boots.

The Black Wind Demon was once a normal black bear, but through cultivating its spirit it was able to become a demon. It frequently visited the nearby Guanyin Hall to discuss religion, and taught the head abbot Jinchi how to preserve his life by tempering his breathing.

When the Black Wind Demon awoke one night and saw the Guanyin Hall burning on the horizon, they quickly flew over to help the monks. They caught sight of a beautiful cassock in the ruins and greedily returned with it to Black Wind Mountain without helping anyone.

entities.description: In Chinese mythology, Chang'e ( CHAHNG-ə; Chinese: 嫦娥; pinyin: Cháng'é), originally called Heng'e (姮娥; Héng'é), is the goddess of the Moon and wife of Hou Yi, the great archer. Renowned for her beauty, Chang'e is also known for ascending to the Moon with her pet Yu Tu, the Moon rabbit and living in the Moon Palace (廣寒宮). She is one of the most prominent goddesses in Chinese folk religion, Chinese Buddhism, Confucianism, and Taoism. In modern times, Chang'e is the namesake of the Chinese Lunar Exploration Program.

entities.name: Chen Guangrui
entities.description:
Born in a small village, Chen Guangrui traveled to Chang'an to take the imperial examination and passed with the highest score. While being paraded on horseback around town, as was customary, he passed the residence of Yin Wenjiao, the daughter of the chief minister. Wenjiao falls in love with him and has the two immediately married.

The following day, the emperor assigned him to be the prefect of Jiangzhou. While travelling, he bought a golden carp to eat, but noticed it was acting oddly and so threw it back into the river. When he had to cross the Hong River, the ferryman Liu Hong beat him to death and threw his corpse in the river so he could impersonate him and force Wenjiao to marry him.

Chen Guangrui's soul would be saved by the Dragon King of Hong River, who as it turned out was the fish that Guangrui had spared. The Dragon King gave Guangrui a Feature-Preserving Pearl to keep his body from rotting, then gave him a job working as an official for him.

Liu Hong was eventually exposed by Guangrui's son, Xuanzang. His family burned Hong's liver at the spot where Guangrui had died, and so the Dragon King resurrected him. Guangrui then returned to Chang'an, where he was promoted to the position of Subchancellor.

Chong'en looked like a young boy. Around him, thousands of beams of light lit up the sky and coloured mists soared. He carried a vase of magical drugs and hung an ancient seal around his waist. A red phoenix and a green phoenix accompanied him.

Sun Wukong came to Fanghu Mountain seeking Chong'en’s help after accidentally knocking down the Ginseng Fruit Tree. Even Chong'en’s strongest elixir wouldn’t be capable of restoring such an important tree, so he sent Sun Wukong on his way.

Little Zhang was born the crown prince of the Flowing Sand Kingdom, but was born under a bad star and was plagued by illness since his childhood. He sought out a teacher, who cured his illnesses with half a pellet and taught him the art of never growing old.

When Sun Wukong came to Xuyi Mountain seeking the help of the Imperial Teacher-King Bodhisattva against the Yellow-Browed Great King, the Bodhisattva instead sent Little Zhang and his Four Great Divine Generals to help. entities.description:
In his role as judge of the dead, Cui Jue wears a black gauze hat with dangling pliant bands, a belt of gold-plated rhinoceros horns, silks robes that emit holy light, and white-soled boots which allow him to walk on clouds. He has luxuriant hair and a flowing beard.

When he was alive, Cui Jue served as the prime minister under Tang Taizong's father. When he died, he was offered the role of a judge under King Yama. When Tang Taizong was killed, he carried with him a letter explaining the situation around his death.

After Tang Taizong was pardoned by the Ten Kings, Cui Jue escorted him through the Underworld to the Sixfold Path of Transmigration.

When Sun Wukong was to be executed, the Old Man of the South Pole ordered the Department of Fire to burn him to death, but it was unable to kill him.

entities.name: Dipankara
entities.description:
Dipankara (Pali: Dīpaṅkara; Sanskrit: Dīpaṃkara, "Lamp bearer") or Dipankara Buddha is one of the Buddhas of the past. He is said to have lived on Earth four asankheyyas and one hundred thousand kalpas ago. According to Buddhists, Dipankara was a previous Buddha who attained Enlightenment eons prior to Gautama Buddha, the historical Buddha.

Generally, Buddhists believe that there has been a succession of many Buddhas in the distant past and that many more will appear in the future. Dipankara was one of these previous Buddhas, while Gautama Buddha was the current and most recent Enlightened one, and Maitreya will be the next Buddha in the distant future.

Chinese Buddhism honors Dipankara as one of many Buddhas of the past. Dipankara, Gautama, and Maitreya are "the Buddhas of Three Times" in Yiguandao.

entities.description:
The is a Dragon King responsible for governing the Hong River.

In the form of a golden carp, the Dragon King was caught by a fisherman and sold to Chen Guangrui. Guangrui noticed the carp was acting oddly, so took it as a sign and threw it back into the river. Later, Guangrui was murdered by Liu Hong, and the Dragon King intervened by taking his soul from the municipal god and making Guangrui one of his staff. When Liu Hong was executed at the site of Guangrui's death, the Dragon King saw fit to resurrect Guangrui.

entities.name: Dragon King of Jing River
entities.description:
The is a Dragon King responsible for governing the Jing River.

The Dragon King of Jing River learned that the fisherman Zhang Shao is receiving tips from the fortune teller Yuan Shoucheng and is enraged. Disguised as a human scholar, he asks Shoucheng about the following days weather. The weather is exactly as Heaven had decreed him to make, so the Dragon King intentionally defies orders to anger the fortune teller.

The Dragon King goes back to Shoucheng's store and wrecks it, but Shoucheng isn't scared as he recognises the Dragon King and knows he will be in trouble. The Dragon King realises what a mistake he's made, and is advised by the fortune teller that Wei Zheng will be sent to execute him, so he should appeal to Tang Taizong.

Tang Taizong agrees, but the Dragon King is nonetheless murdered by Wei Zeng the following day. The Dragon King's ghost attempts to drag Taizong to the Underworld, but is stopped by Guanyin. The Dragon King and several other ghosts then haunt Taizong, causing him to die after seven days.

The Dragon Queen noticed that the Ruyi Jingu Bang began glowing auspiciously when Sun Wukong arrived at the Dragon Palace of the East Sea looking for a weapon. After all the weapons in the palace proved too light for him, the Dragon Queen suggested to her husband Ao Guang that he be given the Ruyi Jingu Bang.

entities.name: Elk Power Immortal
entities.description:
The was one of a trio of supposed Daoist immortals who became preceptors of the Slow Cart Kingdom.

When the Slow Cart Kingdom suffered from drought, the Tiger Power Immortal, Elk Power Immortal, and Antelope Power Immortal arrived and brought rain. They were given the position of preceptor, and used their new station to enslave every Buddhist in the kingdom.

After a ceremony, the three immortals found that all their food offerings had been miraculously eaten. Thinking that the Three Pure Ones did it, they prayed to be given golden elixir by them, and a statue advised them to leave a bottle in the room for it to fill. When the immortals tasted the "golden elixir", they quickly realised it was urine, and the statue turned out to be Sun Wukong in disguise.

The immortals wanted the pilgrims to be enslaved like the other Buddhists, but the king couldn’t figure out who to side with and ordered a series of competitions.

The Equivalent to Tai Sui has pointed teeth, tousled red locks that flared upwards, arrow-like whiskers, and long hair that wraps over his body. Coloured clouds soar up from his head and violent gusts of air burst from his chest,

After killing two peacocks who were children of the Bodhisattva Mahamayuri, the king of Scarlet-Purple Kingdom was ordained to spend three years heartbroken. The Golden-Haired Hou accompanied Guanyin at the meeting where this was decreed and decided to exact the punishment himself.

Becoming the Equivalent to Tai Sui, they went down to the Scarlet-Purple Kingdom and demanded the king's favourite wife be given to them. The kingdom was powerless to resist, so reluctantly gave the queen over to him.

entities.name: Fuxi
entities.description:
Fuxi or Fu Hsi is a culture hero in Chinese mythology, credited along with his sister and wife Nüwa with creating humanity and the invention of music, hunting, fishing, domestication, and cooking, as well as the Cangjie system of writing Chinese characters around 2900 BC or 2000 BC. He is also said to be the originator of bagua (the eight trigrams) after observing that there were eight fundamental building blocks in nature: heaven, earth, water, fire, thunder, wind, mountain, and lake. These eight are all made of different combinations of yin and yang, which are what came to be called bagua.

Fuxi was counted as the first mythical emperor of China, а divine being with a serpent's body who was miraculously born, a Taoist deity, and/or a member of the Three Sovereigns at the beginning of the Chinese dynastic period. Some representations show him as a human with snake-like characteristics, "a leaf-wreathed head growing out of a mountain", "or as a man clothed with animal skins."

While crossing Double-Fork Ridge, Tang Sanzang and his two attendants fell into a pit trap dug by General Yin and his horde of demons. Summoning his allies the Bear Mountain Lord and Bull Scholar, General Yin had the two attendants cooked and eaten, but was unable to kill Tang Sanzang due to his holiness.

When Sun Wukong summoned the Twenty-Eight Constellations to free him from the Golden Cymbals, the Gold Dragon of Neck finally managed to make some indent by shrinking himself, wedging his horn into the seam, and then growing back to size. Sun Wukong uses his Ruyi Jingu Bang to drill a small hole into the horn and transforms into a mustard seed so he can be pulled out.

entities.name: Gold-Crowned Immortal
entities.description:
The is an immortal who runs the Jade Perfection Daoist Abbey at the base of Vulture Peak.

The Gold-Crowned Immortal had a noticeable bald spot and wore a silk gown and sandals. He carried a jade yaks-tail duster and a sacred register.

After being tasked by the Tathagata Buddha to find a pilgrim to retrieve the Tripitaka, Guanyin went down to Jade Perfection Daoist Abbey to seek his advice. The Gold-Crowned Immortal prophesied that Guanyin would encounter four demons during her search for a pilgrim and that she should recruit the demons to be the pilgrims disciples.

14 years later, the Gold-Crowned Immortal greeted Tang Sanzang and his four disciples when they arrived at the base of Vulture Peak. He gave them a vegetarian meal and a scented bath before leading them a short ways up the mountain.

The is a demon who dwelled on Flat Peak Mountain with his brother the Silver Horned King.

The Golden Horned King has round, lightning-flashing eyes and a whiskered face. He wore a tasseled helmet, a coloured belt, a cuirass knit like dragon scales, and a flame-like cape.

The Golden Horned King was one of the apprentices of Laozi, whose job it was to tend Laozi's gold brazier. At the request of the Bodhisattva Guanyin, he and his brother the Silver Horned King were assigned to Flat Peak Mountain to test the conviction of Tang Sanzang when they came through.

When Sun Wukong killed his brother using the Red Gourd, the Golden Horned King armed himself with the Seven Star Sword and the Plantain Fan. He was overwhelmed and retreated to Dragon Suppressing Cave to rally the servants of his late mother, the Dragon Suppressing Great Immortal. He also recruited his uncle, Fox the Seventh.

The is one of the three demons that dwelled in Lion Camel Cave on Lion Camel Ridge. By technicality, he is considered the uncle of the Tathagata Buddha.

The Golden-Winged Great Peng has a leviathan head, leopard eyes with starlike pupils, golden wings, and sharp claws.

When the universe was still forming, a phoenix's egg was inspirited by the creative aura and hatched the Golden-Winged Great Peng and the giant peacock Mahamayuri. Due to Mahamayuri swallowing the Tathagata Buddha when he was young, he is considered the Buddha's spiritual uncle.

The Golden-Winged Great Peng dwelled on Lion Camel Cave along with two other demons. When Sun Wukong invaded their lair in disguise, the Great Peng spotted him when his features momentarily returned to normal and had him trapped in his Yin-Yang Two-Energies Vase, but he soon escaped.

The Great Saint of Nine Spirits is a demon with a lion's head. At first he seems to have only one head, but when he shakes his head his eight other heads appear.

The Great Saint of Nine Spirits is the nine-headed lion ridden by the immortal Taiyi Zhenren. When Zhenren's lion-tamer consumed the Jade Liquid of Transmigration and became drunk for three whole days, the Nine-Headed Lion escaped Wondrous Cliff Palace and went down to earth. He found seven lions living in Nine Bends Cave who became his adopted grandsons.

After his adopted grandson the Yellow Lion Demon was beaten by the pilgrims, he fled to Bamboo Joints Mountain to seek help from the Great Saint of Nine Spirits. Together, they mustered an army which marched on Jade Flower Province.

The Great King of Numinous Power had a broad forehead like a dragon, blazing eyes, sword-like teeth, short and tussled hair, an awl-shaped beard, and carried a pond weed in his mouth. He wore a golden helmet, a gold cuirass that flashed red, a pearl and jade-studded belt, and brown boots.

The Great King of Numinous Power was once the pet goldfish of the Bodhisattva Guanyin. Through constantly listening to Guanyin's lectures, the Great King gained enough numinous power to develop a human form.

The Great King then set himself up as the ruler of Heaven-Reaching River and began demanding a young boy and girl from the nearby Chen Village to eat as payment for bringing them good weather.

In his true form, the Great King of South Hill is a leopard with mugwort-like spots.

The Great King of South Hill was attacked by Zhu Bajie when the pilgrims were travelling through the area, who managed to successfully force him to retreat. After being informed by his servants of the pilgrim’s nature, the Great King of South Hill had three of his servants impersonate him to lure away the three disciples so he could kidnap Tang Sanzang unopposed.

When the pilgrims came to Folded Mountain looking for him, the Great King sent out the skull of another traveller they'd killed and pretended that Tang Sanzang had already been eaten. Sun Wukong eventually discovered the truth and put all the demons to sleep with sleep-bugs, then set the cave on fire. Zhu Bajie then killed the Great King in a single hit.

After which Sun Wukong consented to leave with Taibai Jinxing. However, Sun Wukong was angry at the fact that he was appointed as the Protector of the Horses (i.e., made the stableboy as an insult), and rebelled against Heaven. This led to Taibai Jinxing to once again act as a messenger and somewhat a friend toward Sun Wukong.

The Great White Turtle is an old turtle with a white shell and scabby head.

The Great White Turtle was the local river god of Heaven-Reaching River until he was ousted by the Great King of Numinous Power. After the Great King was defeated, the Great White Turtle offered the pilgrims a ride across the river on his shell.

As they travelled, the Great White Turtle asked Tang Sanzang if he could ask the Tathagata Buddha how long it was going to take to shed his shell and become a human when he finally reached Thunderclap Monastery. Tang Sanzang promised to do so.

entities.description:
The is a demon who impersonated the Princess of India. She turned out to be the that lives on the Moon.

The Jade Rabbit Spirit has shiny red eyes, sharp teeth, divided lips, a creamy straight nose, jade fur, and fleecy feet.

The Jade Rabbit Spirit was once the jade rabbit which pounded the elixir of life for the Star Lord of Supreme Yin. One night, the jade rabbit was slapped by the moon goddess Lady White, an insult she never forgave her for. When she discovered that Lady White had chosen to reincarnate herself as the princess of India, the jade rabbit chose to follow her.

One night, the Jade Rabbit Spirit conjured a strong wind which blew the princess all the way from Shravasti to Jetavana, then assumed her form.

entities.name: Ksitigarbha
entities.description:
Kṣitigarbha (Sanskrit: क्षितिगर्भ, Chinese: 地藏; pinyin: Dìzàng; Japanese: 地蔵; rōmaji: Jizō; Korean: 지장 (地藏); romaja: Jijang; Vietnamese: Địa Tạng (地藏), Standard Tibetan: ས་ཡི་སྙིང་པོ་ Wylie: sa yi snying po) is a bodhisattva primarily revered in East Asian Buddhism and usually depicted as a Buddhist monk. His name may be translated as "Earth Treasury", "Earth Store", "Earth Matrix", or "Earth Womb".  Kṣitigarbha is known for his vow to take responsibility for the instruction of all beings in the six worlds between the death of Gautama Buddha and the rise of Maitreya, as well as his vow not to achieve Buddhahood until all hells are emptied. He is therefore often regarded as the bodhisattva of hell-beings, as well as the guardian of children and patron deity of deceased children and aborted fetuses in Japanese culture.

Usually depicted as a monk with either a halo or a crown bearing images of the Five Tathāgatas around his shaved head, he carries a staff to force open the gates of hell and a wish-fulfilling jewel to light up the darkness.

entities.name: Kui Mulang
entities.description:
Kuimulang (Chinese: 奎木狼; lit. 'The Wood Wolf of Legs') is a deity in traditional Chinese spiritual beliefs. He is considered to be one of the 28 Mansions, which are Chinese constellations. These constellations are the same as those studied in Western astrology. Kuimulang originated from the ancient Chinese worship of the constellations, a spiritual practice that combines Chinese mythology and astronomy.

Kuimulang appears in Chinese mythology and literature, notably in the novels Journey to the West and Fengshen Yanyi. He is linked to a historical figure called Ma Wu, a general who hailed from the town of Huyang in Tanghe, located in the Henan province.

entities.name: Lady Earth Flow
entities.description:
Lady Earth Flow appears at first to be a beautiful woman, but in actuality she is a demon with snow-white fur and a gold nose.

Lady Earth Flow was once an albino rat that gained power by eating sacred flowers and candle wax from Thunderclap Monastery. King Li Jing and Prince Nezha were assigned to lead the hunting party to capture her, and when they caught her the Tathagata Buddha advised them to spare her. She became considered their adoptive daughter afterwards.

When the monk Tang Sanzang came around, Lady Earth Flow disguised herself as a woman tied to a tree and begged him to rescue her. Though Tang Sanzang took Sun Wukong's warning that she was a demon, her persistence eventually broke him down.

They took her to Sea-Pacifying Chan Grove Monastery, where for the next few nights she continuously lured infatuated monks outside and ate them, leaving only their skeletons. She was exposed by Sun Wukong, who had disguised himself as a young monk.

The is a demon who impersonated the king of Black Rooster Kingdom. He turned out to be the belonging to the Bodhisattva Manjushri.

The Azure Lion later returned as one of the three demons that dwelled in Lion Camel Cave on Lion Camel Ridge, making him the only antagonist to trouble the pilgrims in two different circumstances.

In their true form, the Azure Lion has deep green fur, red eyes the size of goblets which emit golden beams, two large ears that flip downwards, a tail as long as a broom, rows of flat teeth, and rounded whiskers His nose curls skywards and flames spout from his brow.

Due to the king of Black Rooster Kingdom unknowingly torturing its master Manjushri for three days, the Tathagata Buddha had the Azure Lion sent to keep the king dead for a period of three years. He also planned it as a test for Tang Sanzang when he came through the area.

entities.name: Liu Hong
entities.description:
Liu Hong and Li Biao operated a ferry service along the Hong River. When Chen Guangrui and his wife Yin Wenjiao booked passage on his boat, Hong was immediately overcome with lust for Wenjiao. He and Biao killed Guangrui, forced Wenjiao to stay as his wife, and then impersonated Guangrui to take his official position as the prefect of Jiangzhou.

Hong's downfall came when Xuanzang, the son of Guangrui and Wenjiao, discovered his heritage and met his mother. He sent word to Wenjiao's father about what he'd done, who quickly mustered an army and arrested Hong. He was executed by having his liver ripped out on the spot where he had killed Guangrui.

entities.name: Mahākāśyapa
entities.description:
Mahākāśyapa (Pali: Mahākassapa) was one of the principal disciples of Gautama Buddha. He is regarded in Buddhism as an enlightened disciple, being foremost in ascetic practice. Mahākāśyapa assumed leadership of the monastic community following the parinirvāṇa (death) of the Buddha, presiding over the First Buddhist Council. He was considered to be the first patriarch in a number of Early Buddhist schools and continued to have an important role as patriarch in the Chan/Zen tradition. In Buddhist texts, he assumed many identities, that of a renunciant saint, a lawgiver, an anti-establishment figure, but also a "guarantor of future justice" in the time of Maitreya, the future Buddha—he has been described as "both the anchorite and the friend of mankind, even of the outcast".

In canonical Buddhist texts in several traditions, Mahākāśyapa was born as Pippali in a village (modern day Pillich which is named after him) and entered an arranged marriage with a woman named Bhadra-Kapilānī. Both of them aspired to lead a celibate life, however, and they decided not to consummate their marriage. Having grown weary of the agricultural profession and the damage it did, they both left the lay life behind to become mendicants. Pippali later met the Buddha, under whom he was ordained as a monk, named Kāśyapa, but later called Mahākāśyapa to distinguish him from other disciples. Mahākāśyapa became an important disciple of the Buddha, to the extent that the Buddha exchanged his robe with him, which was a symbol of the transmittance of the Buddhist teaching. He became foremost in ascetic practices and attained enlightenment shortly after. Despite his ascetic, strict and stern reputation, he paid an interest in community matters and teaching, and was known for his compassion for the poor, which sometimes caused him to be depicted as an anti-establishment figure. He had a prominent role in the cremation of the Buddha, acting as a sort of eldest son of the Buddha, as well as being the leader in the subsequent First Council. He is depicted as hesitatingly allowing Ānanda to participate in the council, and chastising him afterwards for a number of offenses the latter was regarded to have committed.

Mahākāśyapa's life as described in the early Buddhist texts has been considerably studied by scholars, who have been skeptical about his role in the cremation, his role toward Ānanda and the historicity of the council itself. A number of scholars have hypothesized that the accounts have later been embellished to emphasize the values of the Buddhist establishment Mahākāśyapa stood for, emphasizing monastic discipline and ascetic values, as opposed to the values of Ānanda and other disciples. Regardless, it is clear that Mahākāśyapa had an important role in the early days of the Buddhist community after the Buddha's parinirvāṇa, to help establish a stable monastic tradition. He effectively became the leader for the first twenty years after the Buddha, as he had become the most influential figure in the monastic community. For this reason, he was regarded by many early Buddhist schools as a sort of first patriarch, and was seen to have started a lineage of patriarchs of Buddhism.

In many post-canonical texts, Mahākāśyapa decided at the end of his life to enter a state of meditation and suspended animation, which was believed to cause his physical remains to stay intact in a cave under a mountain called Kukkuṭapāda, until the coming of Maitreya Buddha. This story has led to several cults and practices, and affected some Buddhist countries up until early modern times. It has been interpreted by scholars as a narrative to physically connect Gautama Buddha and Maitreya Buddha, through the body of Mahākāśyapa and Gautama Buddha's robe, which covered Mahākāśyapa's remains. In Chan Buddhism, this account was less emphasized, but Mahākāśyapa was seen to have received a special mind-to-mind transmission from Gautama Buddha outside of orthodox scripture, which became essential to the identity of Chan. Again, the robe was an important symbol in this transmission. Apart from having a role in texts and lineage, Mahākāśyapa has often been depicted in Buddhist art as a symbol of reassurance and hope for the future of Buddhism.

entities.name: Manjushri
entities.description:
In the past, Manjushri went to the Black Rooster Kingdom to guide its king towards Buddhism, disguised as a beggar. During her meeting with the king, Manjushri's words disturbed him somehow, and the king ordered that she be hanged in the moat and drowned.

Manjushri remained drowning in the moat for three days before the Six Ding came and saved her. To repay the kings offence, the Tathagata Buddha sent Manjushri's Azure Lion to keep the king dead for three years.

As part of a test for Tang Sanzang and his disciples, Guanyin had Manjushri pose as one of three beautiful brides alongside Samantabhadra and the Old Mother of Mount Li.

After the Azure Lion was defeated, Manjushri came to retrieve it and explain the situation.

entities.name: Mighty Spirit God
entities.description:
The is a god and general of the Heavenly Army.

When Sun Wukong abandoned Heaven, Li Jing and Prince Nezha were sent down to arrest him, and they assigned the Mighty Miracle God as their vanguard. Sun Wukong refused to surrender, so he and the Mighty Miracle God fought. The Mighty Miracle God's axe was broken with just one hit from the Ruyi Jingu Bang, and so he fled like a coward. King Li wanted to have him executed for cowardice, but Prince Nezha convinced him not to.

The Mighty Miracle God was a master of magic, capable of breathing out clouds of mist and scattering clouds of sand from his hand. He wielded a powerful battle-axe named Flower Spreader, which nonetheless proved weak compared to the Ruyi Jingu Bang.

entities.description:
The is the son-in-law of the All-Saints Dragon King.

In his more human-like form, the Nine-Headed Insect looks like a regular human from a distance, but in actuality he has nine faces pointing in each direction. In this form, he wore a white silver helmet, a damask martial robe with cloud patterns, a belt of rhinoceros grain, and two pigskin boots.

In his true form, the Nine-Headed Insect is a twelve-foot long winged snake with nine heads forming a ring, a frame resembling a turtle or iguana, and feathers like a brocade. He has two hook-like legs and eyes which flash beams of golden light.

The Nine-Headed Insect married Princess All-Saints and began corrupting her and her father the All-Saints Dragon King. Due to his influence, his wife stole divine agaric from the Queen Mother of the West's garden in Heaven and his father-in-law stole a [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/%C5%9Aar%C4%ABra sarira] from the Sacrifice Kingdom.

entities.description:
Three days after his son Nezha was born, he proved himself to be a menace by overturning the Dragon King's palace and trying to kill a dragon to use its tendons as a belt. He attempted to kill Nezha, who instead killed himself in rage to return his bones to his father and his skin to his mother.

After dying, Nezha was resurrected by the Tathagata Buddha and eventually began wanting vengeance against his father. King Li Jing pled for mercy from the Buddha, who gifted him a size-changing treasure pagoda filled with openwork carvings and śarīras. Since the pagoda represented the Buddha, Nezhas want for revenge was pacified at the sight of it.

entities.name: Princess Jade-Face
entities.description:
Princess Jade-Face had a coy and beautiful complexion, as pretty as a flower or a jade statue. She had jet-black hair in buns, shining eyes with green mascara, a silk skirt, and small shoes.

Princess Jade-Face was the daughter of a ten-thousand-year-old fox king, and when he died he left his entire fortune to her. With her immense fortune, she was able to convince the Bull Demon King to divorce his wife Princess Iron Fan and marry her instead.

When Sun Wukong came to Thunder-Accumulating Mountain claiming to be an envoy of Princess Iron Fan, Princess Jade-Face insulted her for remaining in contact with her old husband, leading Sun Wukong to angrily insult Princess Jade-Face for buying her marriage. She fled in shock to Sky-Scraping Cave and guilted the Bull Demon King into confronting him.

Later, Princess Jade-Face witnessed the Bull Demon King fight an army of ghostly soldiers by himself and dispatched his army to help. The ghostly army stormed Sky-Scraping Cave, and while the Bull Demon King escaped in the form of a swan, Princess Jade-Face was killed by Zhu Bajie.

The was a weak demon that menaced Tuoluo Village.

The Python Demon was a colossal red-scaled python with flashing eyes, sword-like teeth, golden claws, and a horn of flesh made from carnelian. Morning fog belched from his nose, scarlet clouds covered his body, and putrid fumes wafted off him.

The Python Demon began menacing Tuoluo Village on Seven Extremes Mountain and successfully killed two exorcists they hired to deal with it.

When Sun Wukong and Zhu Bajie came into town, they easily fought the Python Demon back to its hole. Sun Wukong tricked the demon into swallowing him and beat it up on the inside, keeping it out in the day until it died.

entities.name: Qiu Chuji
entities.description:
Qiu Chuji (10 February 1148– 22 August 1227), courtesy name Tongmi (通密), also known by his Taoist name Master Changchun, was a renowned Taoist master from late Southern Song/Jin dynasty and a famous disciple of Wang Chongyang, the founder of Quanzhen School. He is known for being invited by Genghis Khan to a personal meeting near the Hindu Kush, who also respected and honored him as an Immortal.

Qiu is one of the Seven Perfected of the North. He is the founder of the Longmen (Dragon Gate) school of Quanzhen Taoism which already at his time became the most widespread school of Taoism, so prominent that it became synonymous with the phrase "the Dragon Gate covers half the realm", and it is still the case nowadays.

entities.name: Sangha
entities.description:
Saṅgha or saṃgha (IPA: [sɐŋɡʱɐ]) is a term meaning "association", "assembly", "company" or "community". In a political context, it was historically used to denote a governing assembly in a republic or a kingdom, and for a long time, it has been used by religious associations, including Buddhists, Jains, Hindus and Sikhs. Given this history, some Buddhists have stated that the tradition of the sangha represents humanity's oldest surviving democratic institution.

In Buddhism, sangha refers to the monastic communities of bhikkhu (monks) and bhikkhuni (nuns). These communities are traditionally referred to as the bhikkhu-sangha or the bhikkhuni-sangha. As a separate category, those Buddhists who have attained any of the four stages of enlightenment, whether or not they are members of the monastic community, are referred to as the āryasaṅgha ("noble Sangha").

According to the Theravada school and Nichiren Shoshu Buddhism, the term sangha does not refer to the community of unenlightened sāvakas (lay followers) nor does it refer to the community of Buddhists as a whole. Presumably, therefore, they reserve the use of the term sangha for individuals they regard as being enlightened.  The Theravada school uses the term parisā ("assembly") or catuparisā ("fourfold assembly") to refer to the bhikkhu, bhikkhunī, upāsaka, and upāsikā as a collective.

entities.description:
Scholar in a White Robe (白衣秀士, Baiyi Xiushi) is a white snake spirit who was a friend of the Black Wind Demon.

The Scholar in a White Robe visited the Black Wind Demon, alongside Lingxuzi. Initially discussing alchemy, before the Black Wind Demon mentioned his birthday was tomorrow. Afterwards mentioning the fact he managed to find a cassock, and would celebrate by hosting a banquet the day after his birthday, calling it the "Buddha's Robe Banquet".

Wukong, enraged after realizing that the cassock the Black Wind Demon mentioned was his master's, immediately attempted to attack the spirit. Only for the Black Wind Demon to dissipate into black wind, and Lingxuzi to leave via a cloud. Meaning Sun Wukong was only able to kill the Scholar in a White Robe, who reverted back into his true form as a white-patterned snake. With Wukong angrily tearing the body of the Scholar in a White Robe to pieces before he began to search for where the Black Wind Demon went to.

entities.name: Silver Horned King
entities.description:
The is a demon who dwelled on Flat Peak Mountain with his brother the Golden Horned King.

The Silver Horned King wore a phoenix-styled helmet whiter than snow, armour made of bright Persian steel, a belt made from dragon tendons, and goat-skin boots with gaiters shaped like plum flowers.

The Silver Horned King was one of the apprentices of Laozi, whose job it was to tend Laozi's silver brazier. At the request of the Bodhisattva Guanyin, he and his brother the Golden Horned King were assigned to Flat Peak Mountain to test the conviction of Tang Sanzang when they came through.

The Silver Horned King and his minions captured Zhu Bajie while on patrol. They then pretended to be a wounded Daoist in front of the pilgrims, but Sun Wukong assigned himself to carry him and wasn’t fooled. In a panic, the Silver Horned King summoned three mountains to crush Sun Wukong. He then transported the other pilgrims to Lotus Flower Cave.

The Single Horned Rhinoceros King had a single jagged horn, coarse indigo-coloured skin, a long tongue, yellow teeth. He wielded a twelve foot long spotted-steel lance.

The Single Horned Rhinoceros King is the pet buffalo of Laozi. When one of Laozi's apprentices took the Elixir of Seven Returns to the Fire and fell asleep for seven days, the Green Buffalo escaped, taking Laozi's Diamond Cutter with him.

They came to live on Golden Pouch Mountain and set a trap in the form of three beautiful brocade vests in a house of skeletons. Zhu Bajie and Sha Wujing fell for the trap, allowing the Rhinoceros King to capture Tang Sanzang. When Sun Wukong confronted him, the Rhinoceros King used the Diamond Cutter to easily take away his Ruyi Jingu Bang.
